items.statement: The air's aerosol is an input of the air profile in two numbers: its amount, as the extinction at 550 nm, and its kind, as an Ångström exponent from 0 to 2. At the defaults, today's amount and an exponent of 0, every chart holds the bytes it held before. At another amount the lent Sun light and the transmittance chart change with it, and at an exponent of 1.3 the bands take different aerosol, so a profile that gives every band the 550 nm aerosol fails the test. The charts follow a change of either number within the lag the profile declares, and a change of either does not move the environment epoch.

items.statement: A ray that leaves the volume takes the volume's terminal pair once: its sky pixel is `R·L + ΔS`, with `L` the clear sky's radiance there and `(R, ΔS)` the pair the volume itself reports for that ray. With no provider `R` is exactly 1. Where nothing shadows a ray's air, `ΔS` is exactly 0 and the pixel is the clear sky's to the bit. On a ray whose near air a cascade occluder shadows, and on one the registered Sun-path optical depth shadows, `ΔS` is negative and the pixel equals `L + ΔS` at a tolerance the test states. On each of those two rays a sky that takes `ΔS` twice, and a sky left as the clear sky, miss that tolerance: the test runs both through the same comparison and each fails.

items.statement: Scripted CPU schedules show each of the following. Except where a case names a tuning or the Sun's elevation, the Sun stays 10° or more above the horizon, where the Sun tolerance holds its widest value, and a step given as a fraction of a tolerance is that fraction of the widest value. Knob at 1, after initialization: a change of Sun direction or altitude runs all nine stages. With no overlay, or with a registered overlay producer that skips its write, an illuminance-only or colour-only edit runs diffuse alone, and an unchanged frame and a camera cut with identical valid keys each run none. A registered overlay write at fixed light runs exactly diffuse and reflection levels 0–6. An allocated overlay uploaded directly at rebuild, with no registered graph producer, runs those eight on each of two later submissions at fixed camera and Sun direction without further uploads, the first with the light unchanged and the second with solar illuminance halved. Spreading, knob at 4, 6 or 8, on even Sun steps of a tenth of the Sun tolerance: each refresh takes the knob's number of submissions and visits sky view, diffuse and levels 0–6 once in order, with at most 3, 2 or 2 stages on a submission. It keeps its first submission's atmosphere snapshot through phase-edit history resets. A skipped submission retries its stages. After motion stops, the current refresh and outstanding changes drain within the next refresh and the schedule idles. Governed keys, knob at 8, charts settled, camera and Sun direction fixed: with no overlay, an illuminance-only or colour-only edit makes diffuse alone due. With an allocated overlay whose registered producer skips its write, each of those edits makes exactly diffuse and levels 0–6 due. Halving the illuminance runs the eight on that submission, and illuminance steps of a tenth of the light tolerance spread them over eight submissions. Two submissions at zero illuminance count as no change, and a step from zero or to zero runs the due stages on that submission. Choosing, knob at 8: steady steps of 0.3 and of 0.19 of a tolerance per submission choose spreads of 3 and 5, for a Sun step, an altitude step, an illuminance step and a colour step alike, and a step of 0.6 of a tolerance runs every due stage on every submission. Amid Sun steps of a tenth of a tolerance, a refresh that starts on a single step of 1.1 tolerances runs all nine on that submission from that submission's inputs, recorded as a refresh of spread 1 with its change and not as a motion cut, and the refresh after it takes eight submissions. With the knob at 4 and Sun steps of a tenth of a tolerance, a refresh that starts on a single step of 0.4 of a tolerance takes two submissions with at most five stages on each, and the refresh after it takes four. Cutting, knob at 8: when a refresh has run six Sun steps of a tenth of a tolerance and the next step is half a tolerance, that submission runs all nine from its own inputs with motion as its reason, and the next refresh takes eight submissions. Anchors, under the kept tuning whatever values it holds: with the Sun 30° above the horizon, Sun steps of 0.02° choose the knob's value at 4, 6 and 8. With the Sun 30° above the horizon and with it on the horizon, Sun steps of 1.5° run all nine on every submission at 4, 6 and 8. With the Sun 30° above the horizon and the knob at 8, when a refresh is running on Sun steps of 0.02° and the steps become 1.5°, the first 1.5° submission runs all nine from its own inputs with motion as its reason, each 1.5° step after it runs all nine, and the first refresh after the steps return to 0.02° takes eight submissions. Tightening, knob at 8, under a test tuning whose Sun tolerance below a set elevation is a quarter of its widest value, on Sun steps of a tenth of the widest tolerance toward the horizon: when a refresh's eighth submission is the last above that elevation, the next submission starts a refresh of two submissions with at most five stages on each, and on it reflection level 6 still holds the source inputs of the refresh before, 0.8 of the widest tolerance back. When the Sun crosses that elevation on a refresh's fifth submission, that submission runs all nine from its own inputs with motion as its reason. Bound: through the cutting sequence, the 1.1-tolerance and two-submission refreshes, the anchors' 1.5° sequence, both tightening sequences, and Sun steps that rise evenly from a tenth of a tolerance to 1.5° over twenty submissions and fall back over twenty, the source inputs of every readable stage, reflection level 6 included, stay within three widest tolerances of the submission's inputs. Whole updates, knob at 8: first use, a camera cut, generation replacement, a profile epoch, aerosol or night-selection change, and a Sun step over 2° each publish all nine immediately. Knob changes: lengthening the knob finishes the current refresh. Shortening it during motion runs one whole refresh on the first submission at the new value. For six submissions at 6 followed by four at 4, and for an 8-to-6 recovery mid-refresh, each on Sun steps of a tenth of a tolerance, the source submission of every readable stage meets the new tier's 6- or 10-submission bound from the recovery submission onward. Guard: scripted CPU schedules.

work_packages.quality_bar: Sun shadows as in Red Dead Redemption 2's open country, this module's shadow reference since WP6, and as Horizon Forbidden West holds them while its time of day runs: edges that slide and never step, crawl or shimmer, shadows that start at the foot of what casts them, sharper at contact and softer with the blocker's distance, and small shadows that thin out with distance with no line where they stop. Judged in words from the running game against each item's list and beside the takes from before, never against a target image. Grounding is judged in sunlight: the darkening of contact in shade is WP14's, and a cube inside another shadow is not judged here.

items.statement: CPU tests show each of the following. Layout: under the default profile every Sun cascade is a square in the Sun's frame with the same texel count, centred within one of its own texels of the eye. Its half-width is its radius plus a guard band of the same number of texels in every cascade, and each cascade's radius is twice the next finer one's. Every point within a cascade's radius of the eye lies inside its square by at least the guard band, in every direction from the eye, at Sun elevations of 1°, 5°, 35° and 90°. Turning the camera in yaw and pitch, and changing its field of view and its near and far planes, leaves every cascade's matrix unchanged bit for bit. Any camera travel moves a cascade by a whole number of its own texels, zero included. Every caster up-Sun of a cascade's square is inside that cascade's depth range. Profile: `with_sun_shadow_profile(count, reach)` gives `count` cascades, the coarsest of radius `reach` and each inner one half the next; a count of one gives a single cascade of that radius; zero selects the caster height map alone; a count over the engine's full set, or a reach that is not positive and finite, is refused. Bias: no term of the receiver's offset that the shader is given for a cascade is a fixed length; each doubles when that cascade's texel doubles, apart from one floor for the depth format's precision, which the test states. Cast width: the cast width the engine measures from a mesh's triangles is never over, and at most a quarter under, the shortest side of a box, the diameter of a sphere, the diameter of an upright cylinder taller than it is wide, the post's width for a post that carries two thinner arms and whose bounds are over twice that width across, and the shorter side of a flat rectangular sheet. An instance's cast width is its mesh's times its smallest axis scale, and is the same at every Sun direction. Membership: by the rule that decides it, a caster whose cast width is under the threshold, counted in a cascade's texels, is in no pass of that cascade or of a coarser one. That includes the case of design review 1, a caster whose bounds span 1.86 by 4.06 texels in the Sun's frame and whose cast width is 0.6 of a texel. A caster at or over the threshold is in every cascade whose square and depth range it touches. The threshold is at least √2 texels. A caster of an aloft row follows the same rule and is in no pass of the caster height map, and a contribution is asked to draw into every cascade. Coverage: with its cast width equal to the threshold in a cascade, the box, the sphere and the post with arms, drawn on the CPU at that cascade's texel centres, each cover at least one centre at every one of 12 by 12 places of the grid, at Sun elevations of 10°, 35° and 60°. Guard: CPU tests of the fit, the profile, the bias terms, the cast width and the membership rule, which `./dev check` runs from then on.

items.statement: Small Metal tests show each of the following, on scenes of a ground plane and a few casters under the default profile unless a case names another, with every expected answer worked out from the scene's geometry or taken from another run of the scene. Hand-over: for every pair of neighbouring cascades, a box that both hold, whose shadow crosses the distance where one hands to the next, shadows receivers before the blend band, in it and beyond it. Size and blend: for every such pair, a caster whose cast width is at or over the threshold in the finer cascade and under it in the coarser shadows a receiver before the finer cascade's blend band, leaves a receiver beyond the band fully lit, and at three distances across the band its receivers read strictly between the two, lighter with distance. Thin part: a post with arms whose bounds are over the threshold in a cascade and whose cast width is under it casts nothing on a receiver that cascade serves. Steady: a box whose cast width equals the threshold in the cascade that serves its receiver darkens that receiver at each of 16 placements a quarter of a texel apart. Reach by distance: at a 5° Sun, in a view whose profile is one cascade of 128 m, a box of an aloft row shadows a receiver 60 m from the eye. A receiver 500 m from the eye along the Sun's horizontal bearing, which lies inside that cascade's square, with such a box standing in its ray and drawn in the cascade, is fully lit, as it is under a profile of zero cascades. At three distances across the fade before the reach, a receiver in such a box's shadow reads strictly between dark and lit, lighter with distance. A secondary view with that camera and profile reads the same at each of these receivers. Near and far blockers: at a 10° Sun, with a wide box of an aloft row 260 m above the ground and a post that the size rule keeps out of the three coarsest cascades. A receiver the finest cascade serves, 3.5 m outside the edge of the wide box's geometric shadow, with the box's outline wholly outside the finest cascade's square, reads between half lit and 0.95 lit. Across the wide box's shadow edge, 16 receivers a metre apart each differ from the next by at most a fifth. A receiver in the post's shadow at its foot is dark. A receiver two post-widths to the side of the post's shadow reads within 0.05 of the same scene drawn without the post. Culling: under Direct, Frustum and Occlusion the depth read back from every cascade and from the caster height layer equals the Direct route's, with the size rule applied alike. Aloft: a caster of a marked row is in the cascades the size rule gives it and in no texel of the caster height layer, under those three modes. Off camera: a caster behind the camera shades a receiver in view through a cascade, and a caster beyond the reach shades one through the caster height map. Past the reach: a receiver beyond the reach reads the same visibility as the scene drawn with a profile of zero cascades. No history: after a frame drawn at one Sun direction and camera, the next frame at another Sun direction and camera equals, byte for byte, the first frame of a fresh scene at that second state. Guard: small device tests, for what only the drawn depth of each cascade and the shader's choice, blend and two-part read can show.
